properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured), limitation 20, ALREADY RECORDED CLASS, now recurring on the --call door. A PreToolUse guard that matches words anywhere in the command text blocks a door write whose design prose mentions ssh/scp/rsync. reflow2 ships and installs no PreToolUse hook, and none of its hooks reads command text. Matching the executable position passed every door payload and still caught every real remote command in an 8-case probe
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), triage agent D, on limitation 20 of art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02 ("A PreToolUse hook that blocks remote-shell words anywhere in the command text also blocks --call writes whose design text MENTIONS those words").

② PRECEDENT, found by the raw words: fact:root-cause-the-conduct-rule-was-enforced-by-the-projects-own-text-matching-hook-and-reflow2-cannot-say-what-a-rule-guards-2026-09-28 (hxm_program, F-35). That hook's author documented the false positive ("prose in a heredoc ... trips it. Put such prose in a file"). It led to dec:idea-an-enforced-rule-declares-the-action-it-guards-so-enforcement-matches-intent-not-words (open). This is the same class on a new route. Under MCP, design prose travels as tool arguments a Bash guard never sees. Under the door, it travels in the command text.

③ CANDIDATES: (a) the hook is the user's or the organisation's; (b) reflow2 ships or installs it; (c) a reflow2-installed hook matches command text; (d) the door puts the prose where a Bash guard must read it.

⑤ MEASURED (origin/main 66620f7):
- (b) REFUTED. `git grep PreToolUse|permissionDecision` over main finds no shipped or installed PreToolUse hook. reflow2_init.py (ensure_hooks) and reflow2_install.py (install_hooks) register only SessionStart, PostToolUse (matchers mcp__reflow2__.* and Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit) and Stop, all running loop_nudge.py. This machine's ~/.claude/settings.json and the hub's settings hold only those four.
- (c) REFUTED. loop_nudge.py decides by tool_name and tool_input.id/file_path, never by command text.
- (a) HOLDS by elimination. The guard is on the reporter's work machine. Whether it is his own or the organisation's is NOT ESTABLISHED.
- (d) HOLDS. A heredoc or --args '...' carries the prose inside the command string a terminal-tool hook receives.
- Probe (/home/ajs7/.claude/jobs/fa666a94/tmp/triage-D/guard_probe.py, log l20-guard-probe.log), 8 commands:
  - A naive \b(ssh|scp|rsync|mosh|sftp)\b match blocked both door writes whose prose mentioned ssh or rsync (heredoc, and inline single-quoted args).
  - An executable-position match (strip heredoc bodies, shlex-split, split on ; & | ( ), skip VAR= assignments and sudo/timeout/env wrappers with their options) passed both.
  - Both caught all five real remote commands, including env+timeout+ssh, sudo -u + scp, `door && ssh` and /usr/bin/ssh.
  - `--args - < file` passed both, because the prose never enters the command text.

WHAT REFLOW2 CAN OWN: (1) any hook it ships (idea 12) must parse the executable position, never words, and be tested with door payloads; (2) its served door instructions can route prose through a file (`--args - < file`), the workaround the hxm hook's author prescribed; (3) DesignRule vocabulary for what a rule guards (the open decision above). WHAT IT CANNOT OWN: the user's or organisation's guard, and how VS Code hands a terminal command to it (tool_input shape not documented: NOT ESTABLISHED).
